fact_check.claim: Registrar: median grade information is not calculated or made publicly available
fact_check.note: Page says 'Median grade information is not calculated or made publicly available.'

fact_check.claim: The registrar kept recording medians but shares them only with deans, department chairs and people who need them for research
fact_check.note: The registrar page says medians are NOT calculated, which contradicts 'kept recording'; it says nothing about deans, chairs or researchers. The Sun article also does not say this. No source supports the claim.

fact_check.claim: Medians went on the registrar's website in 1998 and on transcripts in 2008; Faculty Senate removed them from the website in 2011
fact_check.note: Sun article confirms 1998 website, 2008 transcripts, 2011 removal from the website.

fact_check.claim: Faculty Senate voted May 11, 2011 after concluding online grade information induced students to select leniently graded courses
fact_check.note: Chronicle article dated May 26, 2011; vote May 11; cites research that online grade information led students to 'select leniently graded courses'. 'induced' is the article's paraphrase, not a verbatim quote problem.

fact_check.claim: Dec. 15, 2023 Faculty Senate approved a resolution ending median grades on transcripts; applies to courses taken Fall 2023 and later
fact_check.note: Sun confirms Dec. 15 approval (Resolution 193) and Fall 2023 and later. Source is a newspaper; an official Faculty Senate or registrar page would be stronger but none was found cited.

fact_check.claim: Faculty Senate's worry in 2011 and again in 2023 was that visible grade data pushed students toward lenient courses
fact_check.note: Both sources cite research that grade information led students to pick leniently graded courses; the Sun does not use the word 'concern' but presents it as the core reason.

fact_check.claim: Jonah Bernard, sophomore in the College of Engineering, January 2024 Guest Room column: without medians students rely on rumors from friends, favoring the well-connected
fact_check.note: Published Jan 29, 2024; author and class year match; argument matches.

fact_check.claim: Christian Baran, sophomore in Arts and Sciences, Nov 2019 Sun column: shouldn't load up on unrelated difficult courses but shouldn't hunt for the easiest classes until graduation; oceanography example
fact_check.note: Author, date, college match. He says hunting for easiest classes until graduation is irresponsible and that taking oceanography is not something he calls out. 'Example worth taking out of genuine interest' is a fair paraphrase.

fact_check.claim: ILR/STSCI 2100 Intro to Statistics: c0rn3lL, Dec 2012, called it the easiest math course anyone can take
fact_check.note: Posted Dec 20, 2012: 'the easiest math course anyone can take at Cornell'.

fact_check.claim: mikeyc765 (2012): non-math statistics courses have a reputation for being easy
fact_check.note: Posted Dec 4, 2012; suggested intro stats from non-math departments may be easier.

fact_check.claim: ILR statistics: monydad, Jun 2018, likely relatively easy, not sure it is the easiest
fact_check.note: Posted June 25, 2018: 'I have reason to suspect that ILR stats is relatively easy'; did not confirm it is the easiest.

fact_check.claim: Psych 101 (Brown_man1987), Sociology 101 (Spanks), DSoc 101 (Brown_man1987 easier than Soc 101; AppleMuncher), Oceanography and Earthquake! (cuapplecider9, not very difficult, fulfilled science requirement), Classic 236 (Biophilic, easy and fun), EAS 268 (laurstar07), all Jul 2008
fact_check.note: All posts dated July 2-4, 2008 and match. EAS 268 poster actually said it was 'soooo much fun!' and recommended it; 'named without comment' is slightly inaccurate but harmless.

fact_check.claim: Same thread mentions mushroom, dinosaurs and Ancient Egypt classes and a warning against Space Exploration without astronomy background
Class Roster filters by distribution requirements, class level, credits and grade option, and can show only classes with syllabi
fact_check.note: All five filters are present on the roster page.

beats_top.why: The #1 result did not load (host not found) and looks like a scraped list; the best readable Cornell sources are old forum threads and the Sun op-ed. Ours is honest about the lack of official data and gives dated, attributed leads, but it is thin on anything current.
changes: Remove the unsupported registrar-sharing claim so the 'why you can't look it up' section is fully sourced.

Make the lead more useful by adding one line pointing students to the Class Roster syllabus filter and the Cornell Sun 'best course' and 'iconic fall classes' pieces as more recent student-voice leads, only if opened and linked.
Optionally link an official Faculty Senate or registrar page for the Dec. 15, 2023 resolution instead of relying only on the Sun.

fixes: In the 'Why you cannot look it up' section, delete the sentence 'The registrar kept recording medians but shares them only with deans, department chairs and people who need them for research.' No source supports it, and the registrar page says medians are not calculated. Replace it with nothing, or with: 'The registrar says median grade information is not calculated or made publicly available.' linked to https://registrar.cornell.edu/about/use-student-data.

In the table, change the EAS 268 comment from 'Named without comment' to 'Called it fun and recommended it for meteorology fans' (source https://talk.collegeconfidential.com/t/credit-filler-courses/520677).
Optional: where the Dec. 15, 2023 Faculty Senate resolution is stated, add a link to an official Cornell Faculty Senate page for Resolution 193 if one can be opened; otherwise keep the Sun link.
